The chapter further narrates blockchain's critical role in trust and transparency within seafood supply chains. The chapter elaborates on the aspects that address pollution, propel economic growth, and promote social equity through IoT, AI, big data, and blockchain.

local_candidates.title: Effect of melamine cyanurate on thermal and flame-retardant behaviour of chopped glass fibre reinforced polyphenylene ether/polystyrene/nylon-6
local_candidates.description: This paper deals with the effect of melamine cyanurate on the thermal and fire retardant behaviour of chopped glass fibre (40 wt.%) reinforced polyphenylene ether/polystyrene/nylon-6 (40/40/20 wt. %) which are processed in a twin screw co-rotating extruder. The composite specimens were fabricated by injection moulding. Addition of melamine cyanurate decreased the amount of toxic gases and organic volatile compounds, crystallinity, crystalline temperature and melt temperature but the same fire-retardant increased glass transition temperature and heat distortion temperature of the ternary alloy. Flame retardancy with V0 and V2 rating along with Limiting Oxygen Index 35% was observed in UL94 test for 5 wt. % and 10 wt. % addition of melamine cyanurate, respectively. Addition of melamine cyanurate increased tensile modulus and elongation at break but decreased the melt flow rate and the moisture content of the ternary alloy.

live_candidates.title: Smart Catfish Aquaculture: An IoT-Based Monitoring and Control System for Continuous Water Quality Management
live_candidates.description: The integration of physical objects with digital systems for automated and continuous monitoring and control has been made possible by advancements in Internet of Things (IoT) technology. Aquaculture is one of the numerous aspects of everyday life where IoT has been widely implemented. Water quality is an important aspect in aquaculture, particularly in catfish farming, as it affects fish growth and survival rates. Temperature, acidity, and dissolved oxygen levels are still frequently measured manually, which can delay decision-making. The aim of this research paper is to design a water quality monitoring and controlling system based on the Internet of Things by using ESP32 as the processor for the system. The major parts of the system are DS18B20 temperature sensor, SEN0161-V2 pH sensor, SEN0237-A oxygen sensor, and ADS1115 analog-to-digital converter. ESP32 analyzes the received data from time to time and transfers the analyzed data to a data processing center through the Wi-Fi connection. There is an actuator used to control the water heater depending on the temperature readings. Implementation results indicate that the system is capable of performing continuous data gathering, transmission, and actuator control with good and consistent performance, leading to efficient and responsive aquaculture water quality monitoring.

live_candidates.title: Smart measurement and monitoring system for aquaculture fisheries with IoT-based telemetry system
live_candidates.description: The instrumentation design of an online monitoring device for aquaculture media is discussed in this article. The main processor in this internet of things (IoT) real-time telemetry system is an ESP32 board. Temperature, acidity level, conductivity level, dissolved oxygen (DO) level, and degree of oxygen reduction in the water were the aquaculture parameters measured. The ESP32 collects data from each sensor, groups it into a dataset, displays it on the LCD, saves it to the SD card, and then uploads it to the real-time database. In addition, an Android application is being developed for users. This device has been tested to ensure that each measured parameter is accurate and precise. The accuracy test, one of the major results of laboratory scale tests, demonstrates that each parameter has a different measurement error that represents with average error absolute. Six tested sensors/instruments were subjected to the test. Average absolute error for temperature sensor is +0.76%, pH sensor is +1.52%, electrical conductivity (EC) sensor is +10.8%, oxidation reduction potential (ORP) sensor is +14.6%, DO sensor is +9.3%, and total dissolve solids (TDS) sensor is +13.2%. This device is very dependable and convenient for monitoring the condition of aquaculture media in real-time and accurately.

live_candidates.title: Smart Aquaculture Monitoring and Automation System Using IoT and Cloud-Based Predictive Analytics

live_candidates.title: IoT-Based Smart BioFloc Monitoring System for Fish Farming
live_candidates.description: To preserve healthy microbial activity and guarantee ideal fish growth, biofloc-based aquaculture systems need exact control over water quality parameters. The risk of ammonia spikes, oxygen depletion, and unstable pH levels is increased by the laborious, time-consuming, and human error-prone nature of traditional monitoring techniques. This project offers an IoT-enabled Smart Biofloc Monitoring System that continuously measures important water parameters in real time in order to address these issues. The system gathers data from several sensors, including as pH, temperature, dissolved oxygen, turbidity, and ammonia sensors, using an ESP32 microcontroller. Wi-Fi connectivity enables the ESP32 to send live readings to the Blynk IoT platform and a web dashboard for remote monitoring, while a buzzer and a 16x2 I2C LCD Provide immediate on-site alerts. To guarantee prompt remedial action, both local alarms and distant notifications are set off when any parameter exceeds its safe level. Farmers may maintain consistent biofloc conditions, lower fish mortality, and increase overall production in aquaculture operations with this cost-effective, scalable, and efficient solution.

live_candidates.title: IOT-Enabled Aquaculture Management System
live_candidates.description: Aquaculture plays a significant role in satisfying the growing global demand for seafood products. However, maintaining optimal water quality and ensuring the health of aquatic organisms remain major challenges for fish farmers. Factors such as temperature fluctuations, dissolved oxygen levels, pH imbalance, and water contamination can significantly affect fish growth and lead to economic losses if not monitored properly. Traditionally, aquaculture management relies on manual monitoring and periodic testing of water quality parameters. These methods are time-consuming, less accurate, and often fail to provide real-time insights, making it difficult to respond quickly to unfavorable conditions. As a result, there is a need for an automated, efficient, and reliable system to manage aquaculture environments. To address these issues, this project proposes an IoT Enabled Aquaculture Management System that provides continuous monitoring and intelligent control of water quality parameters. The system utilizes various sensors to measure key factors such as temperature, pH, turbidity, and dissolved oxygen in real time. The collected data is processed using a microcontroller and transmitted to a cloud platform through IoT technology. Based on the sensor data, the system can automatically control devices such as aerators, water pumps, and feeding mechanisms to maintain optimal conditions for aquatic life. In addition, farmers can monitor real-time data and receive alerts through a mobile application, enabling remote supervision and timely intervention when abnormal conditions are detected. Overall, the proposed system improves efficiency, reduces manual effort, enables real-time monitoring, and enhances productivity in aquaculture operations. By integrating IoT technology with smart automation, the proposed solution aims to ensure sustainable fish farming and maximize yield while minimizing resource wastage. Key Words: IoT, Aquaculture, Water Quality Monitoring, ESP32, Smart Fish Feeder, Firebase, Automation

live_candidates.title: Smart IoT-Based Water Quality Monitoring System for Catfish Aquaculture with AI-Assisted Decision Support
live_candidates.description: Maintaining water quality is essential for catfish aquaculture, where delayed detection can affect fish health and productivity. This paper presents a low-cost IoT-based water quality monitoring system integrating an ESP32 with temperature, pH, total dissolved solids (TDS), and dissolved oxygen (DO) sensors, cloud-based data management, a web dashboard, and rule-based AI decision support. The system was evaluated in a 500-L catfish tank over 30 days. Results demonstrated an average cloud latency of 2.4 s, 99.7% Wi-Fi uptime, 0.12% data loss, and alert delivery within 15–45 s. Sensor measurements achieved 94–97% agreement with laboratory references, while AI-based risk classification achieved 88% expert agreement. These results demonstrate that the proposed system provides reliable real-time monitoring and timely decision support, offering a practical and affordable solution for small- and medium-scale aquaculture farms.

live_candidates.title: An IOT-Based Real-Time Monitoring of Freshwater in Recirculating Aquaculture Systems Integrating Machine Learning
live_candidates.description: This study designed an IoT -based smart monitoring system to address the difficulty of maintaining optimal freshwater quality in recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS). Designing a dependable, automated, real-time freshwater quality parameters monitoring system was the goal. Dissolve oxygen probe, DS18B20 temperature sensor, PH-4502C liquid PH sensor with E201-BNC electrode, ESP32 board, and MQ137 ammonia detection NH3 gas sensor were all employed in the project. The required freshwater parameters of temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen (DO), and ammonia were detected by the integrated sensors. Bayesian machine learning was used to provide alerts and forecast trends in freshwater quality parameters. The machine learning model had high predictive accuracy for temperature, pH, DO, and ammonia, with low error values: MASE (0.5005), RMSSE (0.0509), MAE (0.0371), RMSE (0.0509), and MAPE (40.72%). An R2 value of 0.6231 shows that the model explains variance in the data, which means error metric consistency. The project successfully implemented a functional IoT -based system that provides real-time monitoring of freshwater in RAS in College of Fisheries in Laguna State Polytechnic University Los Banos Campus, ensuring efficient and sustainable aquaculture practices.

live_candidates.title: Development of Real-Time Water Quality Assessment Using eH2O: An Internet of Things-Based Aquaculture Farm Management System
live_candidates.description: Reliable freshwater aquaculture supply chains are crucial for food security and regional economic growth. Poor water quality and delayed management responses can lead to production losses. To tackle these issues, the eH2O system was created as an Internet of Things (IoT) platform for ongoing monitoring of pH, temperature, and dissolved oxygen. This study details the design approach and technical validation of the initial eH2O prototype, tested in the field in Oriental Mindoro. The prototype was assembled based on a structured needs assessment with local farm operators, using an Arduino Mega 2560 and laboratory-grade electrochemical sensors. During verification, the system maintained stable power and data transfer, but mechanical latency (average 15.8 seconds) extended sensor exposure to surface splashes, causing water ingress and electronic failures. Continuous immersion for 72 hours caused signal fatigue, evidenced by a pH change of -0.81. These findings suggest that standard probes and slow actuators are inadequate for long-term pond monitoring. Therefore, a redesigned architecture featuring a dedicated protective housing and an ESP32-based Store-and-Forward system is recommended to enhance resilience and data accuracy in future smart aquaculture systems.

live_candidates.title: An Integrated Wireless Multi-Sensor System for Monitoring the Water Quality of Aquaculture
live_candidates.description: Water temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen (DO), electrical conductivity (EC), and salinity levels are the critical cultivation factors for freshwater aquaculture. This paper proposes a novel wireless multi-sensor system by integrating the temperature, pH, DO, and EC sensors with an ESP 32 Wi-Fi module for monitoring the water quality of freshwater aquaculture, which acquires the sensing data and salinity information directly derived from the EC level. The information of water temperature, pH, DO, EC, and salinity levels was displayed in the ThingSpeak IoT platform and was visualized in a user-friendly manner by ThingView APP. Firstly, these sensors were integrated with an ESP32 Wi-Fi platform. The observations of sensors and the estimated salinity from the EC level were then transmitted by a Wi-Fi network to an on-site Wi-Fi access point (AP). The acquired information was further transmitted to the ThingSpeak IoT and displayed in the form of a web-based monitoring system which can be directly visualized by online browsing or the ThingView APP. Through the complete processes of pre-calibration, in situ measurement, and post-calibration, the results illustrate that the proposed wireless multi-sensor IoT system has sufficient accuracy, reliable confidence, and a good tolerance for monitoring the water quality of freshwater aquaculture.

live_candidates.title: Smart Aquaculture Monitoring Using Autonomous Sensor Networks and Predictive Analytics
live_candidates.description: The sustainability of aquaculture requires constant and precise check-up of water quality parameters to ensure maximum fish well-being and yield. Traditional forms of monitoring are highly manual and reactive leading to delayed response and risk of more operations. This work shows a smart aquaculture monitoring system on the basis of autonomous wireless sensor networks combined with predictive analytics to make proactive decisions. The suggested system utilizes distributed sensor nodes that are used to continuously measure important environmental parameters, such as temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen (DO), and turbidity. The processing unit is edge-enabled and real-time data filters, aggregates, and initial anomaly analyses are done, resulting in less communication overhead and latency. The implementation of a machine learning (Random Forest regression) predictive analytics module is performed to predict the changes in water quality and determine possible risks early in advance. Also, a mathematical representation of the dissolved oxygen dynamics is added to provide more accurate predictions and reliability of the system. Time-series sensor data experimental evaluation shows it can predict with 93.5 percent accuracy with root mean square error of 0.42 mg/L to estimate DO, but has a latency reduction of 35 percent relative to cloud-based methods. The findings confirm that the proposed framework will greatly enhance monitoring effectiveness, facilitate timely response, and sustainably manage aquaculture. The system can provide a scalable and energy-saving platform to the next-generation smart aquaculture systems.

live_candidates.title: An Edge–Cloud Integrated Smart Monitoring System for Sustainable Freshwater Fishpond Management
live_candidates.description: Water quality is a critical determinant of fish health and productivity in freshwater aquaculture, with parameters such as pH, dissolved oxygen (DO), temperature, and turbidity directly influencing growth, metabolism, and disease susceptibility. Traditional monitoring methods, based on manual sampling and laboratory analysis, are often slow, labor-intensive, and unable to detect rapid environmental changes. This paper presents the design and implementation of a hybrid edge–cloud integrated smart monitoring system for sustainable freshwater fishpond management. The system employs an ESP32-based edge node to collect real-time water quality data, detect threshold violations locally, and trigger immediate responses, including LED/buzzer alarms and actuator activation, while simultaneously sending email alerts via SMTP. Long-term data storage, visualization, and remote access are enabled through a cloud platform integrated with MQTT-based data publishing. Experimental evaluation demonstrated a total detection-to-action latency of 3.4 s, local alerts in 1.0 s, email notifications within 7.0 s, and cloud synchronization latency of 150 ms. Sensor measurements achieved high accuracy, with maximum deviations of only ±0.11 pH units, 0.3 mg/L DO, 0.21 NTU turbidity, and 0.2°C temperature. The system maintained 100% uptime during stable network conditions, confirming its reliability for continuous aquaculture monitoring. By combining low-latency local decision-making with cloud-based analytics, the proposed solution enhances operational efficiency, supports proactive management, and aligns with SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) and SDG 14 (Life Below Water). Future work will focus on integrating machine learning models for predictive water quality analysis and expanding the platform to other aquaculture and smart farming applications.

live_candidates.title: Smart Aqua Guard: IoT-Enabled Framework for Real-Time Monitoring and Sustainable Freshwater Aquaculture
live_candidates.description: Freshwater aquaculture plays a vital role in global food security, yet it continues to face challenges such as inefficient feeding practices, unstable water quality, and delayed disease detection. These issues reduce productivity, increase production costs, and create environmental risks. This paper proposes “Smart Aqua Guard” as a solution to these problems that is an integrated aquaculture management framework, a combination of Internet of Things (IoT)-based real-time monitoring, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based analytics, and blockchain-based security. The system uses a distributed sensor network to measure key parameters including pH, dissolved oxygen, temperature, turbidity, and ammonia with data sent to an ESP32 microcontroller to preprocess and send it wirelessly in a secure manner. AI models, such as Random Forest to predict disease, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to predict time-series, and fuzzy logic to optimize feeding are produced to generate proactive insights and automated control reactions. Immutability and traceability of operational data is guaranteed by a blockchain layer, which increases trust and compliance throughout the aquaculture supply chain. A case study of Tilapia farm in Bangladesh reveals that the farm had realized high level of improvement such as reduced mortality risk by 22 %, increased feed ratio by 15, and response time was improved more than 90 % as compared to when they operated manual. These results indicate the power of Smart Aqua Guard, an intelligent, scalable and sustainable concept of freshwater aquaculture management.

live_candidates.title: IoT Aquaculture System Prototype

The present Paper provides an extensive review of the research about the combination of IoT and AI in the aquaculture, especially in the context of water quality. Monitoring, automatic feeding, and the creation of a smart management framework are the main areas of concern. The review also mentions the attempts made in the experimental setups incorporating ESP32 and Arduino, where the cloud systems have been utilized for inland-based aquaculture. The aquatic health monitoring and controlling parameters were pH, temperature, turbidity, and ammonia. With the help of IoT, the environmental parameters within which the aquatic turnovers are kept have been controlled with a very high level of precision. Hence, the decrease of turnover lowers the requirement for manual interventions that in turn support sustainability. Thus, the review presents the evolution of smart aquaculture, assesses the current installations in terms of their merits and demerits, and paves the next step in aquaculture as the continuation of the journey.
